result.summary: The remote agent handled the patient's request clearly and consistently, explaining both options for scheduling an appointment for an adult family member and the authorization requirement. Clarification was provided when the patient asked about the process, and all claims were supported by the conversation. Next steps were actionable and relevant. No concerns were identified in patient coherence, but turn-taking and ending require audio review for full assessment.

dimensions.rationale: Agent directly addresses the patient's request about who can arrange an appointment and explains the process and requirements for both options.

evidence.quote: You can arrange an appointment for an adult family member. I'll just need to verify your authorization to speak on their behalf before we continue.

An adult patient can call us directly to arrange their own appointment. If you want to schedule for them, you'll just need to confirm you're authorized to do so when you call. Either option works, whatever is easier for you and your family member.
If your family member calls themselves, the process is usually quicker and smoother. If you call for them, just be ready to confirm you're authorized to help with their care.
